title: Filet crochet motif
subtitle: A lace grid motif worked from a chart of filled and open squares
excerpt: Filet crochet builds a grid of open chain squares with treble posts, filling selected squares with extra trebles to form a pattern from the contrast between filled and empty cells. Any image that reads as a pixel grid — letters, simple animals, geometric shapes — can be translated to a filet chart and crocheted.
sourceNotes: Filet crochet is one of the oldest documented crochet techniques; it appears extensively in Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886) and Weldon's Practical Crochet from Volume 1 (1885) onward.
heroPrompt: A filet crochet square motif in fine white cotton thread on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. A simple heart chart visible in the filet grid, open cells against filled treble cells, 10 cm square.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished filet motif measures 10 × 10 cm in 4-ply cotton with a 2.5 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Filet crochet motif
chartDefinition.caption: Open cell: 2 tr + ch 2. Filled cell: 4 tr. Heart chart shown: 9 cells wide × 9 rows deep.

glossaryTerms.definition: The basic unit of a filet grid. An open cell is two trebles with a chain-2 space between them. A filled cell is four trebles with no gap. Combining open and filled cells creates patterns from their contrast.

content.text: Filet crochet builds patterns by alternating open and filled

in a regular grid. An open cell is two trebles with a chain-2 gap; a filled cell is four trebles with no gap. The chart reads like a pixel grid — shaded squares are filled cells, white squares are open. Any pattern that works as a pixel image translates directly to filet.

This motif uses a simple 9 × 9 heart chart. Block the finished piece firmly — wet-blocking opens the chain spaces and gives the grid its characteristic crisp lace appearance. Without blocking, the chain spaces collapse and the pattern is hard to read.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 8 g of 4-ply cotton thread. A 2.5 mm hook. Blocking mat and pins.

content.text: Foundation chain: ch 29. (9 cells × 3 ch per cell + 2 turning ch.)
Row 1: tr in 4th ch from hook. *Ch 2, skip 2 ch, tr in next ch.* Rep across. Turn. (9 open cells.)

Row 2 onward: ch 5 (counts as tr + ch 2). *For open cell: tr in next tr, ch 2. For filled cell: tr in each of the 2 skipped ch, tr in next tr (4 tr total, no ch 2).* Work per heart chart rows 1–9. Fasten off.
Work the bruges lace tile for a different lace construction using strip-based rather than grid-based assembly.
